content.title: About
content.content: Brussels sprouts are small, cabbage-like vegetables belonging to the cruciferous family. They originated in the Mediterranean region but are now cultivated in many temperate areas worldwide. Raw sprouts have a mildly bitter, nutty flavor and a crunchy texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The vegetable is named after Brussels, where it was first cultivated in the 16th century.
It is one of the richest sources of vitamin K among vegetables.
Brussels sprouts contain glucoraphanin, a compound that may support the body’s detoxification processes.
Eating them raw preserves more vitamins than cooking.
In the 19th century Europeans often referred to them as “little cabbage.”

items.title: High in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate is needed for DNA synthesis and is especially important during pregnancy.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: The sprouts contain glucoraphanin and other polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Cruciferous vegetables can cause increased gas production in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Interaction with blood thinners
items.content: High vitamin K intake may reduce the effectiveness of anticoagulant medications.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Rarely, some people may experience an allergic reaction to Brussels sprouts.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Raw sprouts can become contaminated with bacteria if not stored properly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw Brussels sprouts can be thinly sliced into salads, blended into smoothies, or used as a crunchy topping. They can also be lightly marinated in olive oil, lemon juice, and spices for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the sprouts in the refrigerator in a perforated bag or a ventilated container. Properly stored, they stay fresh for 1‑2 weeks. Discard any wilted or yellowing heads.
